title: Theo and the Debt
premise: Xanthe Vasquez, a crash investigator who lost their family in the unexplained downing of Flight 447, has spent years buried in cases airlines want forgotten. When a burner phone rings with the voice of their sister—presumed dead for six years—they learn she survived, was recruited by the syndicate that caused the crash, and is now the key witness a defector named Ilse Brandt can expose. Xanthe must smuggle Ilse across a border checkpoint before the night shift changes and the syndicate's cleaners arrive, all while deciding whether trusting the voice on the phone will save them or finish what row twelve started. The story ends at the checkpoint: Ilse crosses, the sister's sacrifice exposes the syndicate's ledger, and Xanthe finally buries their family for real.
about_author: Tamsin Joubert is a former aviation insurance adjuster who spent a decade reading wreckage reports before turning to fiction. She writes from a farmhouse outside Bloemfontein, where she keeps a wall of unsolved air disaster clippings.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Opening on a routine crash-site inspection in the Karoo, Xanthe catalogs debris with clinical detachment until a seat fragment numbered twelve forces the memory of Flight 447 back up. Emotional beat: grief held under professional frost, cracking at the seams.

chapters.title: The Burner
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. A package arrives with no return address containing a cheap phone; at 3 a.m. it rings and a voice Xanthe knows intimately says only, 'Don't hang up.' Emotional beat: vertigo—the dead speaking, hope weaponized against skepticism.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe runs acoustic analysis obsessively, comparing the call to old home videos, while their handler Marisol warns them off 'ghost cases.' Emotional beat: obsession as anesthesia; the first hint Marisol may not be an ally.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Weighs
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Following coordinates texted to the burner, Xanthe finds a storage unit holding Flight 447 maintenance records proving sabotage—and a second file labeled BRANDT, I. Emotional beat: vindication curdling into terror; they were meant to find this.

chapters.title: Ilse
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Introducing the defector in a safehouse near the border town of Vioolsdrif, a former syndicate accountant who memorized the ledger and now waits, terrified, for extraction. Emotional beat: cold competence masking a woman running out of time.

chapters.title: The Sister Problem
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The caller admits she is Nadia Vasquez—alive, coerced into the syndicate after surviving the crash, and offering Ilse's location in exchange for extraction. Emotional beat: joy poisoned by the realization that Nadia is also bait.

chapters.title: Marisol's Shadow
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe tails their own handler and watches her meet a syndicate fixer named Corven; the agency has been selling attribution—deciding which disasters stay accidents—for years. Emotional beat: betrayal; the ground under Xanthe's whole career gives way.

chapters.title: Two Nights to Vioolsdrif
chapters.summary: POV alternating Xanthe/Ilse. Xanthe drives north while Ilse endures a syndicate sweep of the safehouse network, hiding in a freezer truck. Emotional beat: parallel dread converging; found family begins forming through radio static.

chapters.title: The Farmhouse
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe and Ilse meet, distrust crackling; Ilse tests Xanthe with details only the ledger would know, then hands over a microfilm copy sewn into her coat lining. Emotional beat: wary alliance, two survivors recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Corven Calls
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Corven contacts Xanthe directly, offering Nadia's real location in exchange for Ilse—and reveals Nadia's survival was engineered to lure exactly this extraction. Emotional beat: duty versus love made literal; Xanthe refuses, lying to themselves about why.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse maps the border crossing: day shift is corrupt but slow, night shift is syndicate-paid but thin between 2:40 and 3:10 a.m. Emotional beat: methodical courage; Ilse chooses to trust Xanthe with the plan and her life.

chapters.title: Nadia's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. On the burner, Nadia confesses she helped falsify the 447 report under duress, believing Xanthe would never survive the truth. Emotional beat: rage, forgiveness half-granted; love against duty fully ignited.

chapters.title: The Tail
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. A gray sedan follows them from Upington; Xanthe runs a counter-surveillance dance through river towns, losing it at the cost of their last clean identity documents. Emotional beat: hunted intimacy; Xanthe and Ilse become co-conspirators in earnest.

chapters.title: Safehouse Gospel
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Waiting out a storm, Ilse tells the story of how she turned—her brother died on 447 too, unlisted, undocumented. Emotional beat: found family sealed by shared mourning; the mission becomes personal for both.

chapters.title: Marisol's Warning
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Marisol breaks cover to warn that Corven has moved the checkpoint shift change up to midnight and that Nadia is being transported to the crossing as leverage. Emotional beat: ambiguous loyalty—is this redemption or the final hook?

chapters.title: The Decoy Road
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe splits the plan: a decoy vehicle runs the main crossing while they take the old pontoon ferry downstream. Emotional beat: high-wire tension; every choice spends someone's safety.

chapters.title: Pontoon
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. The ferry crossing goes wrong when floodwater drags the cable; Ilse nearly drowns saving the microfilm, and Xanthe pulls her out. Emotional beat: sacrifice made flesh; trust becomes love neither names.

chapters.title: Midnight Shift Change
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. They reach the checkpoint as Corven's men seal it early; Nadia steps out of a black SUV, alive and held at gunpoint, forced to call Xanthe forward. Emotional beat: the trap springs; everything converges.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. In the standoff, Nadia turns Corven's gun aside long enough for Ilse to broadcast the ledger to three news desks; Corven shoots Nadia as the border lights die. Emotional beat: climax—love costs everything, and pays anyway.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Attributed
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. With the ledger public, Flight 447 is reclassified as sabotage; Marisol testifies, Corven's network unravels, and Xanthe identifies Nadia's remains with steady hands. Emotional beat: hollowed-out justice; grief finally given a name and a grave.

chapters.title: What Ilse Carried
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse, granted asylum, unpacks the coat lining and finds a second thing Nadia hid there years ago: letters to Xanthe, written during captivity. Emotional beat: tenderness after ruin; the dead still giving gifts.

chapters.title: Theo and the Debt
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. At a small graveside service, Xanthe reads one letter aloud, adopts the stray dog Nadia once wrote about—Theo—and accepts that survival is a debt paid forward by living visibly. Emotional beat: resolution; invisible no more, carrying the found family home.
